extractions.source_title: Black Rot of Brassicas | NC State Extension Publications

disease_name.evidence: Black rot is a disease of brassicas ( Brassicaceae ) that occurs worldwide and can result in high losses of yield and quality.

pathogen_scientific_name.evidence: The disease is caused by the seed-borne bacterium Xanthomonas campestris pv. campetris .

type_of_disease.evidence: The disease is caused by the seed-borne bacterium Xanthomonas campestris pv. campetris .

affected_parts.evidence: Root crops may not have visible symptoms on above ground tissues, but blackened veins will develop on the roots. As the disease progresses and spreads to the stem, the inner tissue becomes black and the flow of water and nutrients is inhibited leading to plant death.

summary.value: Yellow, v-shaped lesions extending toward the base of the leaf that eventually lead to wilt and necrosis, with distinct blackening of veins within lesions and adjacent areas.
summary.evidence: The most common symptom of black rot are yellow, v-shaped lesions that extend toward the base of the leaf that eventually lead to wilt and necrosis.

diagnostic_features.value: Distinct blackening of veins within lesions and in adjacent areas is indicative of black rot; bacterial streaming (a stream of white substance exiting plant tissue placed in water) is a good indicator of bacterial infection.
diagnostic_features.evidence: However, within lesions and in adjacent areas, distinct blackening of veins indicative of black rot may occur (Fig. 1).

look_alikes.evidence: Symptoms can appear similar to drought stress, overwatering, or excessive fertilizer application.
